ai.description: *Sphaerotheca breviceps* is a stout, 4–6 cm frog with a rounded snout. It is brown or olive with a pale vertebral stripe and possesses shovel-shaped metatarsal tubercles for efficient burrowing.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sphaerotheca breviceps* is best distinguished by its distinct, shovel-shaped inner metatarsal tubercle, which is significantly larger and more prominent than in other species.
ai.habitat: The Indian burrowing frog inhabits moist deciduous forests, grasslands, and agricultural fields, typically found in low-lying areas up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Indian Burrowing Frog spends most of the year underground, emerging only during monsoon rains to feed on insects and engage in explosive breeding.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sphaerotheca breviceps* breeds during the monsoon season, laying large clutches of up to 3,000 eggs in temporary rain pools. It is an explosive breeder.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sphaerotheca breviceps* is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the arid plains of Pakistan to the humid regions of India and Sri Lanka.
ai.callDescription: The Indian Burrowing Frog produces a series of short, low-pitched, metallic "tink" or "chuck" sounds, typically heard from flooded fields or burrows during the monsoon.
